overview: The root causes are: (1) all three DB adapters lack a batch string-fetch method `db.mget`, blocking batch confirmation-code lookups; (2) `sendValidationEmail` stores no `expires` timestamp in the confirmation object, so all downstream expiry checks fall back to unreliable `db.pttl`; (3) `getEmailForValidation` does not exist, leaving the admin validate/resend handlers unable to resolve a pending-confirmation email; (4) `loadUserInfo` never attaches `email:pending`/`email:expired` flags; (5) `User.validateEmail` and `User.sendValidationEmail` socket handlers bypass the new retrieval step; (6) `deleteAccount` never calls `expireValidation`. The fix proceeds in dependency order: add `mget` to all three DB adapters → add `expires` to confirmation objects and update expiry-reading helpers in `email.js` → add `getEmailForValidation` → update `loadUserInfo` with `getConfirmObjs` → update socket handlers → add `expireValidation` to the delete path.

src/database/redis/main.js:60 -- return await module.client.get(key) -- single-key string fetch; mget counterpart would be return await module.client.mget(keys)

edits.change_rationale: Multiple violations: (1) req-009/req-010: sendValidationEmail writes no `expires` field — must add `expires: Date.now() + (emailConfirmExpiry * 60 * 60 * 1000)` to the db.setObject call at lines 139-142. (2) req-012: isValidationPending never checks expiry; once `expires` is stored, it must fetch confirmObj in the no-email branch too and check `Date.now() < confirmObj.expires`. (3) req-013: canSendValidation / getValidationExpiry use db.pttl instead of the stored timestamp; getValidationExpiry should read confirmObj.expires, and canSendValidation must add a null/negative guard falling back to Date.now() when TTL is unavailable. (4) req-011/req-015: getEmailForValidation is entirely absent — must be added using getUserField as first-try and the confirm:byUid→confirm:code chain as fallback, with UID-match guard before returning confirmObj.email.

edits.change_rationale: req-001/req-002: loadUserInfo (lines 163-185) contains no logic to attach email:pending or email:expired flags. Must add a getConfirmObjs() inner helper that (a) calls db.mget on the array of confirm:byUid:<uid> keys, (b) calls db.getObjects on the resulting confirm:<code> keys, and (c) returns the indexed confirmation objects. getConfirmObjs() should be wired as a fifth entry in the existing Promise.all block, matching the existing parallel-fetch pattern. Each user object must then be enriched with email:pending and email:expired derived from the returned confirmation objects and their expires timestamps.

src/controllers/admin/users.js:163-172 — existing Promise.all pattern in loadUserInfo; getConfirmObjs() should be added as a fifth parallel call

edits.change_rationale: req-006/req-007: User.validateEmail (lines 62-70) calls confirmByUid directly without first resolving the email via getEmailForValidation or persisting it via setUserField. User.sendValidationEmail (lines 79-80) passes only { force: true } with no email option. Both handlers must be updated: validateEmail must call getEmailForValidation(uid), conditionally call user.setUserField(uid, 'email', email), then confirmByUid; sendValidationEmail must call getEmailForValidation(uid) and pass the resolved email as an option to sendValidationEmail.

edits.change_rationale: req-008: User.deleteAccount (lines 141-152) never calls user.email.expireValidation(uid), leaving confirm:byUid:<uid> and confirm:<code> keys orphaned in the DB after account deletion. expireValidation already exists at src/user/email.js:63 and is used in other cleanup paths (reset.js:125, profile.js:330). It must be added to the Promise.all block in deleteAccount, parallel to the existing User.reset.cleanByUid(uid) call.
